1. Turn on the Accessibility service
Android lets apps without device-admin rights turn off the screen only through an Accessibility service. In Accessibility settings open \"Able screen lock\" and turn it on.
It reads only the window structure of the system interface to know when the lock screen is showing. Nothing is stored or sent.
Able Accessibility service

What it does: sends Android's "lock screen" action when you ask for it (tool, tile, widget or double tap).

What it reads: only the window structure (view IDs) of the system interface (SystemUI), to know whether the lock screen, notification shade or PIN pad is showing. It does not read what you type or the content of other apps, and it stores or sends nothing.

Risk: Accessibility services are powerful; Android shows a warning when you turn one on. With the lock-screen option, Able places an invisible area over the upper part of the lock screen and replays your swipes so unlocking keeps working.

How to turn it off: Android Settings › Accessibility › Able screen lock, or the button on this screen.
2. Choose where to double tap
Turn on the Accessibility service first.
Lock screen
Double tap empty space in the upper part of the lock screen.
Lock the phone and wake it to check that the lock screen is recognised.
The lock screen was recognised the last time it was shown.
The lock screen was not recognised last time: double tap may not work there on this device or Android version.
Double tap on the lock screen

While the lock screen is showing, Able places an invisible area over its upper two thirds (clock and notifications). Two taps on empty space turn off the screen. Taps on buttons and notifications are passed on, and swipes are replayed so you can still unlock or open the shade.

The area is disabled automatically when the notification shade, PIN, pattern or password screen is visible, or when Able cannot recognise the lock screen. It never covers the fingerprint sensor or the bottom shortcuts.

Limits: long presses and some animations on the lock screen may feel different. Recognition depends on the system interface and may stop working after an update.

How to turn it off: switch this option off, or turn off the Accessibility service.
Home screen widget (recommended)
No widget placed yet.
Add widget to home screen
Your launcher does not let apps add widgets. Long-press empty home space › Widgets › Able › \"Double tap to lock\".
Confirm in the dialog, then resize the widget over empty home space.
The launcher did not accept the request. Add the widget manually from the widget list.
Double tap on the home screen

Android does not tell apps where you tap on the launcher's home screen, so the reliable way is an invisible, resizable widget: place it on empty home space (for example a whole empty page or the area between your icons) and double tap it to turn off the screen. It works with every launcher that supports widgets.

The widget does nothing else and reads nothing. If the Accessibility service is off, a tap on it opens this screen.

How to remove it: long-press the area and drag it to "Remove".
Status bar
Double tap the status bar while using the phone. Off by default.
Double tap on the status bar

While the phone is unlocked, Able places an invisible strip over the status bar. Two taps turn off the screen; a swipe down still opens the notification shade.

The strip is disabled in fullscreen apps and while the shade is open. Status-bar icons are not tappable through it.

How to turn it off: switch this option off.
Gesture settings
Maximum time between taps: %1$d ms
Time between taps

Two taps count as a double tap only if the second arrives within this time. Increase it if double taps are missed; decrease it if single taps lock the screen by mistake. Use the practice area to try it without locking.
Vibrate before locking
A short vibration confirms the double tap.
Practice area: double tap here to try the timing
Double tap recognised
Practice area for the double tap timing. It does not lock the screen.
Test
Turn off the screen now to check that locking works on this device. Then try the double tap in each place you turned on.
Other ways to lock
The Quick Settings tile locks with one tap from the notification shade and uses the same Accessibility service.
Depends on your device

Recognising the lock screen depends on the system interface (SystemUI), and the home-screen options on your launcher. They may stop working after an Android or launcher update; Able then stops intercepting touches rather than blocking the screen. Android can also block Accessibility services from apps outside the Play Store or on managed devices (for example with Advanced Protection or work policies); then none of these options work.
home screen (double tap)
Home screen without widget
Double tap empty home-screen space.
Off. The widget above is the reliable option.
Active: double tap empty space on the home pages.
Go to the home screen to start it.
No default home app found: choose one in Android settings.
Android refused the invisible watcher on this device. Use the widget.
Double tap on the home screen without a widget

Able never holds, delays or replays your touches, so scrolling between home pages and opening apps work exactly as usual. An invisible 1×1 pixel watcher only learns when a touch starts, not where. When two touches start within the time set below while your home app shows its home pages, Able waits a moment: if the home app reported no icon tap, long press or page swipe, the screen turns off. Before turning it off Able checks again that the home pages (not the app list, a folder or the notification shade) are in front.

Limits: Android does not tell Able where you tapped, so two very quick taps next to an icon, or a tap right after a swipe, can be misread. With home apps that are not based on Launcher3, Able only checks that the home app is in front.

Nothing you touch is stored or sent. It works only while the phone is unlocked. To turn it off: switch this option off.
